title: Article 13 — Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of Fundamental Rights

content.overview: Article 13 makes laws inconsistent with Part III void to the extent of the inconsistency. It is the textual foundation for judicial review of legislation on Fundamental Rights grounds. Pre-Constitution laws and post-Constitution laws are both addressed; doctrines of severability and eclipse operate within this framework.

sections.heading: Voidness to the extent of inconsistency
sections.body: Inconsistent law is void to the extent of the inconsistency — not necessarily the entire statute if severable portions can stand.

sections.heading: Judicial review
sections.body: Courts examine whether a law or State action infringes Part III. Article 13 does not replace Articles 32 and 226 as remedial gateways; it supplies the rule of inconsistency.

sections.heading: Historical and current
sections.body: Pre-Constitution laws inconsistent with Part III are not enforceable to that extent (eclipse may apply so that the law revives if the inconsistency later disappears — verify doctrine against controlling authorities). Post-Constitution laws that contravene Part III are void to the extent of the contravention.

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Identify the law, the Part III article engaged, and the relief under Article 32 or 226. Argue severability if only part of the statute is challenged.
